structural_changes.rationale: C2's members are all the same defect in different cells of one walker: `_v2_fingerprint` `continue`s past non-dict tables/columns (_json_shred.py:117-127) so two structurally-different on-disk configs collapse to one `schema_fingerprint` and a stale per-port cache is judged fresh; `shred_to_buffers` flattens a nested list inside a scalar array (the recursive `_walk` list arm at :600-618 re-descends, inflating rows past the source element count with zero accounting); `_resolve_leaf` collapses a mid-walk list to `cur[0]` and discards the rest (:533) silently. The codebase ALREADY built the right machinery for this exact mandate — `ShredSkipStats` with `count_record_skip`/`count_row_skip`, surfaced in meta.json and the build response (_json_shred.py:184-220, 593-639) — but it is applied unevenly: object-vs-scalar shape mismatches are counted (:628-632) while nested-list flattening and mid-walk-list collapse are not, and the fingerprint path bypasses accounting entirely. The structural fix is to make conservation a checked INVARIANT, not a per-site convention: every place the walker can drop or multiply an input must either raise or route through `count_*_skip`, and `build_per_port_cache` must assert `sum(emitted_rows) + skip_stats.total == reconcilable_source_count` (or, where exact reconciliation is infeasible, that every mid-walk list collapse is counted). Because the named wave-2 mandate is 'no silent loss + fingerprint completeness', encoding it as a build-time reconciliation check means a future walker edit that re-introduces silent loss fails a test instead of shipping. The fingerprint half is dissolved by removing the defensive `continue`s: a malformed table/column must raise (validity already routes ApiInputSchemaError to 422 via build_per_port_cache's validate_v2_schema), so two distinct configs can never hash equal.
structural_changes.dissolves: C2 in full (5 members: fingerprint collision on non-dict tables/columns, nested-list row inflation, mid-walk-list collapse, the status/validity-path schema-validation gap, and the data-file stat-gate — the latter two by the same pass). Structurally generalizes to C5 (parser silent structure loss) and C7's catch-all laundering: the same 'fail-loud-or-account at every loss boundary' discipline is the codebase-wide fix for the heat-map #2 + fail-loud-mandate cluster, so adopting it as a checked invariant here sets the pattern the parser raises and the trace de-laundering follow.

Batches naturally with C11 (same file, committed-mirror lock/rename) and C12 (json_cache.py duplicate-key). No external branch touches _json_shred.py; serialize against in-flight wave-2 `_walk` edits.
structural_changes.risk: Low-to-medium. The reconciliation assertion needs a precise definition of 'expected rows' for legitimately-repeated arrays (an array of N objects SHOULD emit N rows to its path's table — that is correct multiplication, not loss), so the invariant is 'every DROP and every COLLAPSE is counted', not 'rows == records'. The fingerprint raise changes a previously-silent acceptance into a 422 for genuinely malformed on-disk configs — desired per fail-loud, but pin with a test that a hand-corrupted config now raises rather than collides. Always-hash data-file matching is the only real perf cost (re-hash on every validity check); the stat-gate-as-hint-then-verify variant keeps the fast path while closing the byte-preserving-rewrite hole.
structural_changes.sketch: 1) In `_v2_fingerprint`, replace `if not isinstance(table, dict): continue` and the column equivalent with `raise ApiInputSchemaError(...)` (callers already validate first, so this only fires on a genuinely malformed on-disk config). 2) In `_resolve_leaf`, when a mid-walk value is a list with len>1, raise or thread a skip count rather than silently taking `cur[0]`. 3) In `shred_to_buffers._walk`, when a scalar-array element is itself a list (nested), count a row skip for that table instead of re-descending and inflating. 4) In `build_per_port_cache`, after the shred, assert that `total_emitted + skip_stats.total` reconciles to the counted source elements at each emitting depth and fail the build (atomic temp-dir already rolls back) if not — making conservation a tested property. 5) In `routes/json_cache._v2_status_response`, add `validate_v2_schema(v2_config)` before `is_per_port_cache_valid`. 6) Decide the data-file policy: simplest is to drop the mtime fast-path and always compare sha256 in `_data_file_matches` (:269-271). structural_changes.title: Fold artifact identity into one fingerprint helper and thread the resolved artifacts through BOTH the deploy validate path and every output-affecting cache key, so a model can never be fingerprinted-out or validated-against-a-different-build
structural_changes.rationale: C3 and C4 are the same structural gap on the deployed/served pricing path — the only HIGH findings that touch real production prices — seen from two sides. C3: `infer_output_schema` keys its `.haute_cache/output_schema.json` on `graph_fingerprint(graph, output_node_id, *input_node_ids)` only (deploy/_schema.py:95-103), which by construction excludes model-artifact bytes/version (`_graph_base_fingerprint` hashes node configs + edges, not artifact files — _cache.py:191-218); a retrained in-place 'latest' artifact bakes a stale ModelSignature/manifest. C4: `score_test_quotes` and `infer_output_schema` both call `score_graph(...)` WITHOUT passing `resolved.artifacts` (deploy/_validators.py:375-380; deploy/_schema.py:134-139) even though `score_graph`/`score_graph_lazy` accept `artifact_paths` (deploy/_scorer.py:844-859,423-457) and the container DOES pass them (`_container.py:394,407`); so the 'test before live' gate loads a model live from MLflow that can differ from the bundled bytes the container serves. The shared root is that artifact identity is not a first-class input to either the fingerprint or the validation wiring. The structural fix is one helper — `artifact_identity_fingerprint(resolved.artifacts)` reusing the existing `haute.execution._stat_gated_runtime_path_fingerprint` (already used by deploy/_scorer.py:199) — and ONE rule: every code path that resolves artifacts threads `resolved.artifacts` into both (a) `score_graph(..., artifact_paths=...)` and (b) the cache key. Doing both in one pass through deploy/_schema.py avoids touching the file twice and makes 'validate loads byte-identical artifacts to serve' and 'output-schema cache invalidates on artifact change' true by the same construction. This is the existing fingerprint-COMPLETENESS dossier applied to the artifact input class the keys currently miss.

structural_changes.title: Add a parse-time STRUCTURE-CONSERVATION pass that proves every authored node/edge/submodel survives into the graph (or raises), making the parser fail-loud by construction rather than per-shape
structural_changes.rationale: C5's seven members are one class: the parser drops or collapses authored graph structure at many independent boundaries WITHOUT a loud error, violating the CLAUDE.md fail-loud mandate. Duplicate decorated function names collapse to one GraphNode.id (executor then silently loses the first node's pricing body); `async def` nodes are invisible to the AST walker; the regex fallback discards ALL submodels on any main-file syntax error; two submodels resolving to one pipeline_name overwrite; an implicit param-name edge into a submodel child is dropped; nested submodel calls are ignored; aliased-import preamble over-captures. Today each is a separate silent gap to be patched individually and re-introducible. The structural change is a single post-parse CONSERVATION pass that the parser ALWAYS runs: it counts the authored surface (top-level decorated function defs incl. AsyncFunctionDef, `connect()`/param-name edges, and `pipeline.submodel(...)` literals — recoverable by the same regex scan the healthy path uses for submodels) and asserts each maps to exactly one element in the resulting PipelineGraph, raising a ParseError naming the offending function/file on any collapse, overwrite, or drop. This converts 'silent loss at shape X' from a whack-a-mole of per-site patches into one invariant check, so a future parser change that loses structure fails the conservation assertion instead of shipping. The regex fallback's blanket submodel-null is fixed under the same umbrella by reusing `resolve_submodel_reference` in the fallback path (the cluster's fix_strategy), so the fallback recovers submodels exactly as the healthy path does.
structural_changes.dissolves: C5 in full (all 7 members: regex-fallback submodel discard, duplicate-name collapse, async-def invisibility, implicit cross-boundary edge drop, submodel name-collision overwrite, nested-submodel silent ignore, aliased-import preamble over-capture — the conservation pass catches the structural ones loudly; the regex-recovery + alias-aware boundary detection close the two that need a specific fix). Directly enforces the codebase-wide fail-loud principle on heat-map #5, the same principle C2/C7 adopt, so it is the parser arm of one cross-cutting discipline.

No external branch overlap on parser files.
structural_changes.risk: Medium. The conservation pass must distinguish a LEGITIMATE structural transform (a submodel placeholder intentionally not present as a root node; `output`/`dataSink` shapes) from a genuine loss, so it needs an explicit allowlist of 'authored element -> expected graph element(s)' rather than naive count-equality — get this wrong and it false-positives on valid graphs. The async-def and duplicate-name policies are product decisions (raise vs support): the cluster recommends raise for duplicate-name and either-broaden-or-raise for async; pick raise for both to stay strictly fail-loud and pin each with a failing test first. The regex-fallback recovery must not itself raise on the very syntax error that triggered the fallback — it recovers submodels around the broken main file, so scope its parsing to the submodel literals only.

structural_changes.title: Replace the trace layer's value/position correlation heuristics and `except Exception`-to-row-value laundering with a sound, fail-loud display contract (uniqueness + scale-relative + structural-target; no catch-all fallback)
structural_changes.rationale: C7 and C8 are one class on the trace/explanation path: the waterfall shown to actuaries is computed by UNSOUND post-hoc heuristics whose failures are then LAUNDERED into self-consistent-looking-but-wrong numbers, violating fail-loud (display-only — never corrupts a stored price, but presents a wrong 'calculation' as authoritative). C7: `_expression_parser` reimplements Polars semantics and returns wrong/None for concat_str/replace_strict/unsupported ops, while `_compute_result` and the parse/evaluate/compute/chain layer wrap everything in `except Exception` and fall back to `row_values.get(target_column)` (the raw observed value), so the evaluator bug renders as a clean waterfall. C8: `_correlate_rows_posthoc` has a positional fast-path that attaches the wrong parent row when a same-row-count transform reorders rows and shares no columns; `_fix_upstream_values` relocates by a FIXED 1e-6 ABSOLUTE tolerance that collides distinct small-magnitude factors; the waterfall membership gate drops a real multiplicative step that is a row-local no-op. The shared root is that correlation/evaluation trades soundness (uniqueness, scale-relativity, structural targeting, loud failure) for convenience, and a catch-all hides the result. The structural change is to make the trace display layer fail-closed by construction: (a) delete the value-laundering catch-alls so a failed evaluation/correlation surfaces as an explicit 'unresolved' marker or a typed ExpressionEvaluationError, never as the observed value masquerading as the computed one; (b) replace position/absolute-tolerance heuristics with the uniqueness + `rel_tol=1e-9` (mirroring the existing `_trace_values_match`) + structural-target rules already partly present elsewhere in the trace code. Encoding 'no silent fallback to the observed value' as the contract means a future evaluator gap shows up as a loud 'unresolved', not a plausible wrong number — the same fail-loud discipline as C2/C5 applied to the display path.

Eliminates heat-map #7's 'wrong explanation shown loudly-clean' as a class and closes the trace arm of the fail-loud-mandate cross-cutting concern.

The main care is that removing the catch-alls must not turn a genuinely-non-fatal, legitimately-unresolvable row into a hard 500 on the trace endpoint: surface it as an explicit per-step 'unresolved' status the UI renders, not an exception that aborts the whole waterfall — the contract is 'never show the observed value AS the computed value', which an 'unresolved' marker satisfies without crashing. A test must assert that a deliberately-introduced evaluator gap (e.g. an unsupported op) surfaces as 'unresolved'/raises rather than as a self-consistent wrong waterfall — this is exactly the missing 'does any test assert a systematic evaluator bug surfaces loudly' guarantee (architecture open question #8).

structural_changes.title: Make every stateful NodeType a single config-driven runtime helper that BOTH the executor builder and the codegen template call (kill the passthrough-template class)
structural_changes.rationale: haute's defining correctness obligation is that the executed graph and the generated standalone file price identically. The codebase ALREADY proves the right pattern for half the node types: banding/ratingStep/modelScore emit a body that calls a shared helper in haute.graph_utils (apply_banding_from_config / apply_rating_step_from_config / score_from_config) — the SAME function the executor's _builders.py calls — so equivalence is structural, not a coincidence to be re-verified per node type. The bug class C1 is entirely the SECOND pattern: optimiserApply/optimiser/modelling/scenarioExpander/liveSwitch emit bodies that do NOT call the executor's logic. I confirmed this directly: codegen.py:304-365 only rewrites the passthrough `return <first>` to `return <ratebook_input>` and NEVER calls the executor's _dispatch_apply/_apply_ratebook (_builders.py:1375-1429), so the standalone file returns the un-optimised frame; _codegen_builders.py:398-417 plus the _make_passthrough_builder factory (line 784) literally formalize 'emit a no-op body' as a reusable pattern (the _OPTIMISER/_OPTIMISER_APPLY/_MODELLING/_SCENARIO_EXPANDER templates are all `return {first}`); and liveSwitch hard-wires 'live' in the template (_gen_live_switch, line 521) while the executor routes by ctx.source. The root reason a no-op body even RUNS as a no-op is that pipeline.py's Node.__call__ (lines 54-68) is a generic frame-router with NO NodeType dispatch (no NODE_REGISTRY lookup) — so the body IS the implementation. The structural fix is to delete the divergent second pattern: give each stateful type one apply_*_from_config(first, *, config, base_dir, source=...) helper in the shared graph_utils layer that runs the identical dispatch, and have the executor builder AND the codegen template both call it. This eliminates the entire 'generated body ≠ executor builder' class (3 cluster members + the whole heat-map #1 / cross-cutting #1 concern) by construction and prevents recurrence: a new stateful NodeType physically cannot ship a no-op body, because there is one implementation to call.

Also removes _make_passthrough_builder and the bespoke codegen.py rewrite helpers (_optimiser_apply_ratebook_return_source, _rewrite_single_return_source) as dead code.

structural_changes.title: Collapse the four duplicated job-failure-mapping ladders in _optimiser_service.py into one shared exception-to-terminal-reason handler
structural_changes.rationale: The 5045-LOC optimiser god-file's single worst duplication is a ~70-line exception ladder that maps backend exceptions (ExecutionMemoryLimitExceededError, HTTPException w/ memory-limit detection, BoundedMemoryUnsupportedError, ValueError, bare Exception) to a (terminal_reason, http_status, job-update) transition. I diffed the two largest copies: _run_frontier_auto_range_job (lines 3567-3638) and _run_streaming_frontier_auto_range_job (lines 3858-3929) are byte-identical EXCEPT two log-event string literals ('frontier_auto_range_bounded_streaming_unsupported' vs 'frontier_auto_range_streaming_bounded_streaming_unsupported'). A third, drifted variant lives in the solve launcher (2789-2829) and a fourth partial in _record_http_setup_failure's call sites. This is precisely the drift hazard the heat-map (#4) and open-question #12 call out: 'have all 4 duplicated failure-mapping copies stayed in sync?' — they already have NOT (the BoundedMemory log strings differ; the solve copy hand-rolls the memory-limit branch the helpers exist for). A single change to this duplicated machinery (the exact ask of C10/C15) means future fixes to one copy silently skip the others. Centralizing it kills the drift class and makes the file shorter and the lifecycle transitions provably uniform. Crucially this is a behaviour-preserving extraction: the half-built helper layer (_memory_limit_job_update, _http_exception_job_update, _http_error_job_update at 310-368, and _record_setup_failure at 3335) already exists — the duplication is in the EXCEPT-CLAUSE WIRING that calls them, not the helpers, so the extraction is low-risk.

structural_changes.title: Delete the value-laundering catch-alls on the trace display path: make the expression evaluator and step enricher fail-loud (or return an explicit unresolved sentinel), never the observed row value
structural_changes.rationale: The trace subsystem violates the CLAUDE.md fail-loud mandate in a way that is structurally self-concealing: _expression_parser.py is a parallel re-implementation of Polars semantics, and _compute_result (lines 1528-1539) wraps the whole evaluation in `except Exception: return row_values.get(target_column)`. That means whenever the re-implementation is wrong or incomplete (confirmed gaps: concat_str/horizontal funcs, replace_strict with no default, unsupported ops at lines 995/1304/2028/2151), the evaluator silently returns the ALREADY-OBSERVED price for that column — producing a waterfall that looks perfectly self-consistent while showing actuaries a fabricated 'calculation'. The same laundering repeats at the orchestration layer: enrich_steps (line 1363) is one giant per-step try/except whose docstring openly states 'if a per-step enrichment fails, the fields stay None' (best-effort), so a systematic enricher bug degrades EVERY trace with no signal. This is a single structural defect — a catch-all that substitutes the input for the computed output — replicated at evaluate/compute/chain/enrich layers. Removing the substitution (propagate a typed ExpressionEvaluationError; on the orchestration layer, mark the step result as an explicit 'unresolved' rather than silently None) converts a whole class of 'wrong-but-clean explanation' bugs into loud, testable failures, and makes the known operator gaps (C7) surface in CI instead of hiding. Open-question #8 ('does any test assert a systematic evaluator bug surfaces loudly?') is currently answered 'no' precisely because of these catch-alls.

structural_changes.title: Replace projection fan-in / passthrough column-ownership GUESSING with operand-derived ownership, and make every non-strict fall-through carry a typed ProjectionReason (no silent column drop)
structural_changes.rationale: projection.py (2505 LOC) is the column-demand planner that bounds what batch/deploy actually read — a wrong demand prunes a needed column and silently mis-prices. Its fan-in logic is built on layered HEURISTICS rather than the true Polars operand, which is the shared root of the whole C9 class. I confirmed the structure: PolarsFanInRule.parent_demands (lines 1427-1522) tries simple_left_join_passthrough_parent(joins) and, failing that, unambiguous_passthrough_parent(parent_inputs, referenced) (line 1494-1499) — i.e. when columns aren't covered by an explicit join, it ROUTES ALL of them to a single heuristically-chosen parent and only raises if even that guess is unavailable. The same guess-shaped logic recurs in codegen's _format_contract_source (single-stale/single-unmatched re-attribution) and in compute_prepared_plan's non-strict branch, which can drop a caller-supplied seed for a >1-child opaque node with no diagnostic (the file's default profiles are non-strict, so the drop is silent in exactly the common case). These are three faces of one structural weakness: fan-in/passthrough ownership is INFERRED rather than read from the join's actual left/right operand, and the non-strict fall-throughs are unobservable. The fix that kills the class is to make ownership evidence-based (the join's left operand is the true owner of un-suffixed collision columns; if that can't be determined, fail loud with ContractMismatchError as the strict path already does) and to attach a distinct ProjectionReason to every implicit-else so a drop becomes diagnostic data, not silence. ProjectionReason already exists as the mechanism (lines 67-97, used densely at 2169-2467) — the gap is that the heuristic fall-throughs bypass it.
structural_changes.dissolves: C9 in full (PolarsFanInRule subset-heuristic routing a column to a non-producing parent; codegen _format_contract_source mis-attribution; compute_prepared_plan silent seed drop). Closes the 'fan-in column ownership inferred by heuristic instead of from the Polars operand' class and the 'non-strict projection fall-through is silent' class — making projection mispruning either correct-by-operand or loud, never silently wrong.

No external branch overlap; if proposal 1 defers behind branches, the codegen.py change here is in a different function and can proceed independently.

Mitigate by: (1) preferring 'widen the demand to a provably-safe superset' over 'raise' where a correct wider bound exists (the audit's explicit guidance — edges+body remain the source of truth, so projection can fall back to a wider-but-correct bound rather than erroring); (2) reserving the hard ContractMismatchError for the genuinely-ambiguous join case; (3) gating with tests that construct a same-row-count reorder + zero-shared-column fan-in and assert the column is routed to the true left operand (or a loud error), plus a >1-child opaque-seed graph asserting the seed is preserved or the drop carries a projection_seed_dropped reason.

structural_changes.title: Make the codegen body's config-faithfulness a typed registry obligation, not a convention — every NodeType declares an `apply_<type>_from_config` runtime helper that BOTH the executor builder and the generated body call (kills C1 entirely)
structural_changes.rationale: The integrity spine (`_registry.py`) already enforces 'exactly one exec fn AND one codegen fn per NodeType' at import (`validate_registry_complete`). But that invariant is too weak: it guarantees a codegen builder *exists*, not that its emitted body is *config-faithful*. For banding/ratingStep/modelScore the body calls a shared `apply_banding_from_config`/`apply_rating_step_from_config`/`score_from_config` (in `_rating.py`/`graph_utils`), so the standalone `Node.__call__` path (pipeline.py:54 — `self.fn(*dfs)`, with NO `NODE_REGISTRY` dispatch) reproduces the executor. For optimiser/optimiserApply/modelling/scenarioExpander the body is `return {first}` (a pure passthrough, `_codegen_builders.py:391-417`), and for liveSwitch it hard-wires the 'live' branch (`_codegen_builders.py:521-539`). 'Passthrough-body-ness' is thus an invisible property of a string template that no type or test can see — the exact illegal state my lens targets. The current patch is worse than a gap: `codegen.py:_optimiser_apply_ratebook_return_source` + `_rewrite_single_return_source` do a fragile *string rewrite* of the return line that only fixes frame SELECTION for the ratebook case and never applies the artifact at all. structural_changes.title: Make cache identity a TOTAL function of all output-affecting inputs by routing every fingerprint through one `output_identity(...)` contributor registry — close the model-artifact, preamble-sys.path, and v2-schema-completeness leaks structurally
structural_changes.rationale: `_cache.py` already centralises the digest ENCODER (`canonical_json` is 'THE only one', `graph_fingerprint` is `v5:`-prefixed). But it does not centralise the digest INPUT SET: each call site decides which inputs to mix, and three of them omit an output-affecting class. `graph_fingerprint` mixes node configs + edges + preamble-utility bytes, but NOT bundled model-artifact bytes/version (so a retrained 'latest' artifact bakes a stale ModelSignature/output schema — C3); `preamble_execution_fingerprint` hashes only `pipeline_dir`/cwd `utility.py` candidates and misses a utility resolved elsewhere on sys.path (C3); `_v2_fingerprint` in `_json_shred.py` (108-147) `continue`s past non-dict tables/columns so two structurally-different on-disk configs collapse to one `schema_fingerprint` (C2), and the status route reads the config WITHOUT `validate_v2_schema` (C2). The unifying defect is that 'what counts as an input to the identity' is implicit and per-site, so omissions are invisible. A single `CacheIdentity` contributor protocol — each output-affecting input class registers a `contribute(graph, ctx) -> digest-material` and the key is the canonical_json of ALL registered contributors — makes 'I forgot to include the model artifact' a missing-contributor assertion rather than a stale-cache-served-as-fresh bug.

Prevents the RECURRENCE class: any new cache key that forgets an input class fails the contributor-completeness check instead of silently colliding. Pairs with C12 (single duplicate-key JSON read) since both are 'two code paths decide identity for one artifact'.

structural_changes.title: Make the rating-key canonicalisation dtype-faithful end-to-end by carrying the source dtype across the trace/save boundary, so the Python mirror, the Polars twin, and the ratebook save-vs-apply sides cannot disagree (eliminates the silent neutral-1.0 miss class)
structural_changes.rationale: `_rating.py` deliberately keeps ONE key form via the Python mirror `normalise_rating_key` (309-343) and the Polars twin `_rating_key_expr` (346-370), pinned by `test_rating_key_agreement.py`. But the agreement is explicitly DTYPE-INCOMPLETE: the mirror widens non-integer Float32 to Float64 (`pl.Series([value], dtype=pl.Float64)`, line 342) while the twin canonicalises in the column's native Float32 (line 354), and the docstring itself concedes 'non-integer Float32 ... sit outside the enrichment-agreement guarantee' because 'their dtype is lost at the trace JSON boundary'. Separately, ratebook factor levels are canonicalised at SAVE time against the banding-source column dtype but APPLIED against the optimiserApply input column dtype (`routes/_optimiser_service.py` + `_builders.py`), so a Float32-vs-Float64 divergence for the same logical factor yields a join miss → silent neutral 1.0 / default rate → wrong applied price. Both are the same root: canonicalisation is not pinned to a single, carried dtype. The structural fix is to make dtype a first-class part of the key boundary — thread the factor column's original dtype through the trace JSON (so the mirror canonicalises via `pl.Series([...], dtype=<carried>)`, matching the twin exactly) and assert/enforce save-vs-apply dtype agreement — so 'mirror and twin agree' becomes total instead of dtype-restricted.

structural_changes.title: Dtype-faithful rating-key differential: drive the Python mirror and Polars twin from the SAME real Polars column dtype, parametrized across the full dtype matrix
structural_changes.rationale: C6 is a silent neutral-1.0 / default-rate mispricing, and I found the existing test is structurally incapable of catching it. `test_rating_key_agreement.py::test_known_canonical_forms` (L267-270) DOES diff `normalise_rating_key(value)` against `_expr_canonical(value)` — but `_expr_canonical` (L259-263) builds `pl.Series('k',[value])` from a Python value, so a Python float is ALWAYS inferred as Float64; and the mirror `normalise_rating_key` (L342) ALSO casts via `pl.Series([value], dtype=pl.Float64)`. Both sides use Float64, so they agree by CONSTRUCTION — the test can never observe the divergence. The real engine twin `_rating_key_expr` (L354-368) casts the column at its NATIVE dtype, so a Float32 column takes the Float32→Utf8 path, which differs from Float64→Utf8 for many values. The test file's own docstring concedes the hole: 'non-integer Float32 keys are outside the enrichment-agreement guarantee' (L26, L330-333). That carve-out IS the bug class. The structural fix is to make the differential dtype-FAITHFUL: feed both the mirror and the twin from one canonical Polars column of an explicit dtype, and parametrize the dtype.

structural_changes.title: Make `graph_utils` the COMPLETE codegen runtime facade: one `apply_<type>_from_config(first, config=, base_dir=)` per behavioural NodeType, called by BOTH the executor builder and the generated body
structural_changes.rationale: haute already HAS the right architecture for half its node types and abandons it for the other half. `graph_utils.py` is the curated public runtime surface generated code imports (its module docstring literally says 'the intentional import surface ... that generated pipeline code needs at runtime'). For banding/ratingStep/modelScore the generated body calls a shared, config-driven helper (`apply_banding_from_config`, `apply_rating_step_from_config`, `score_from_config`) AND the executor builder (`_builders._build_*`) funnels through the SAME helper — so the saved-file path and the canvas path are one implementation, and the README promise ('it's just Python ... everything you've built still works') holds by construction. For liveSwitch/optimiser/optimiserApply/scenarioExpander/modelling, codegen instead emits a literal `return {first}` passthrough (`_codegen_builders.py` `_LIVE_SWITCH`, `_OPTIMISER`, `_OPTIMISER_APPLY`, `_MODELLING`, `_SCENARIO_EXPANDER`) while the executor builder does the real work (`_build_optimiser_apply` loads the artifact and dispatches; `_build_live_switch` branches on `_scenario_ctx`). `Node.__call__` in pipeline.py has NO NodeType dispatch — it blindly calls `self.fn`, so a standalone `pipeline.run()` of the saved file executes the passthrough and silently mis-prices. The structural cure is to FINISH the existing pattern rather than invent a new one: every behavioural NodeType gets a `graph_utils` helper that is the single shared implementation, eliminating the entire 'codegen template diverges from executor builder' class. The infrastructure to support this already exists — `_config_io.config_path_for_node` already maps these very types to sidecar filenames (LIVE_SWITCH→source_switch, OPTIMISER_APPLY→apply_optimisation, ...), so the generated body can read its config the same way banding does; and `_scenario_ctx` is a contextvar that `Pipeline.run()`/`Pipeline.score()` already set, so the live/batch branch flows into the helper with zero extra plumbing.

structural_changes.title: Replace the structural round-trip property test's 'config keys match' equivalence with an EXECUTION-equivalence oracle, and make it the gate every NodeType must pass
structural_changes.rationale: The reason C1 stayed latent is that haute's strongest safety net — the Hypothesis round-trip property test — asserts the WRONG invariant for the dangerous node types. `test_parser_roundtrip.py` (lines 543-574) verifies that after codegen→parse the node's *config dict keys* survive (`assert parsed.get(key) == orig.get(key)` for liveSwitch's input_scenario_map, optimiser/optimiserApply/scenarioExpander/modelling keys). Structural fidelity of a node whose generated BODY is `return {first}` is necessarily satisfied — so the test is green precisely where the engine mis-prices. The architecture doc names the system's 'defining correctness obligation' as *semantic* equivalence between the two execution modes, yet there is no property asserting that obligation for the skipped types (open-question #1 answers itself: there is none). The structural fix is to upgrade the equivalence relation the property test enforces from 'same config shape' to 'same output frame', for ALL node types, so the property test becomes a true fixpoint over BEHAVIOUR. This converts an entire class of future codegen/executor drift from 'silent wrong price in a saved file' into 'red CI on the PR that introduces it' — the highest-leverage DX change because it makes the equivalence contract executable and self-enforcing.

structural_changes.title: Introduce a single `ResolvedArtifacts`-threaded `score_graph(..., artifacts=)` seam so deploy validate, deploy serve, and output-schema inference are the SAME call
structural_changes.rationale: The deploy path has the identical shape of defect as C1 — two call sites that should be one make independent artifact-resolution decisions — and it touches the LIVE served price, so through a DX lens it is the more urgent instance of the same structural smell. `score_test_quotes` (the 'test before live' gate) calls `score_graph(graph=..., input_df=..., input_node_ids=..., output_node_id=...)` with NO `artifact_paths` (_validators.py:375), so validation loads the model live from MLflow (`version='latest'`, mutable) while the container serves the bundled artifacts (`_container.py` passes `artifact_paths=_artifact_paths`); `infer_output_schema` (_schema.py:74) likewise resolves no artifacts and keys its cache on `graph_fingerprint` alone (line 95), baking a stale ModelSignature when a 'latest' artifact is retrained in place. The structural fix is to make 'which artifacts this scoring run uses' a REQUIRED, explicit parameter of one scoring entrypoint — a `ResolvedArtifacts` value object already implied by `resolved.artifacts` in the deploy config — and route validate, serve, and schema-inference through that one seam. Then 'validate scored a different model than we serve' becomes structurally impossible: the artifact identity is the same object, and (folding C3) it participates in the schema cache key. This is the 'make the contract explicit in the type signature' move a staff engineer reaches for — the divergence was possible only because `artifact_paths` defaulted to None and a caller could forget it.

structural_changes.title: Promote the generated standalone file to a first-class, documented runtime contract: a `haute.runtime` public API + a `# generated by haute` provenance header that the README's portability promise points to
structural_changes.rationale: The README sells a load-bearing developer promise — 'Your pipelines are Python files ... If you ever want to stop using Haute, everything you've built still works - it's just Python' — but the generated file's runtime dependencies are an UNDOCUMENTED, private-looking grab-bag: bodies import from `haute.graph_utils` (a facade whose name doesn't signal 'this is the stable runtime ABI'), call helpers like `apply_banding_from_config`, and rely on the `_scenario_ctx` contextvar being set by `Pipeline.run()/score()`. A staff engineer extending haute, or an actuary auditing a saved pipeline, has no signposted contract telling them which imports are guaranteed-stable, what `pipeline.run()` vs `pipeline.score(df)` mean, or that the file is generated. The structural change is to NAME and DOCUMENT the standalone-runtime contract: (a) expose a `haute.runtime` namespace (re-exporting the `*_from_config` helpers + `Pipeline`) as THE public surface generated code targets, so the 'codegen ABI' is an explicit, versioned thing rather than an implicit set of underscore-adjacent imports; (b) emit a provenance header in every generated file linking to that contract and stating the run/score entrypoints; (c) document the live/batch contextvar semantics so a standalone caller knows how to select the branch. This turns the portability promise from prose into an enforced, discoverable API — and it gives change #1 a natural home (new behavioural helpers land in `haute.runtime`, and a public-API test can assert that EVERY symbol a generated body imports is exported from `haute.runtime`, catching the next private-import leak).

Converts the README promise into a testable contract (a meta-test: every import in any generated body resolves to a `haute.runtime` export). Improves error ergonomics across the board by giving the standalone path a documented surface where helper functions can raise typed `HauteError`s with the same `**context` rendering the rest of the codebase uses (errors.py), instead of bare `ValueError`/`RuntimeError` that a portability-minded user hits with no guidance.

structural_changes.title: Collapse the dual NodeType decorator/exec/codegen registration into one declarative `@node_type(...)` table so behaviour, codegen, columns, and the public decorator are defined together
structural_changes.rationale: haute's integrity spine is the `NODE_REGISTRY` ('exactly one exec AND one codegen builder per NodeType, validated complete at import'), and it correctly fails loud on a missing entry. But the THREE things a NodeType needs are still authored in three disconnected places: the public decorator (`Pipeline.optimiser_apply` etc. in pipeline.py, ~20 near-identical 3-line methods), the exec builder (`@_register(NodeType.X)` in _builders.py), and the codegen builder (`@_register_codegen(NodeType.X)` / `_assign_codegen` in _codegen_builders.py). Nothing structurally binds 'this decorator' to 'this exec builder' to 'this codegen body', which is exactly how a behavioural type (optimiserApply) ended up with a real exec builder and a passthrough codegen body that nobody flagged — the registry checks PRESENCE, not EQUIVALENCE of intent. A staff-level refactor unifies these into a single declarative registration so adding/auditing a node type is one cohesive unit, and the 'is this type behavioural or passthrough?' fact (which change #1 and #2 both need) is recorded ONCE and machine-readable. This is the deeper structural root under C1: the engine's two halves are wired by convention across files rather than co-located by construction.
structural_changes.dissolves: Attacks the ROOT shared by C1 (and the recurrence vector behind it): 'exec builder and codegen builder for one type are authored apart and can encode different behaviour'. Makes the behavioural/passthrough classification a first-class registry attribute that change #2's meta-test and change #1's shared-helper requirement can both read, so the system can ASSERT 'every behavioural type shares a runtime helper between exec and codegen' at import time — turning a code-review judgement into a structural invariant. Also shrinks pipeline.py's ~20 boilerplate decorator methods to a generated set, reducing the public-API surface drift class.

Fold in C3's two sibling members the same way: resolve the preamble utility via `importlib.util.find_spec` under exec-time sys.path and hash `spec.origin` into `preamble_execution_fingerprint` (`_cache.py`); drop `id(scoring_model)` from the feature-validation key (`_model_scorer.py`) and rely on contract+schema. Add a regression test asserting validate and serve load BYTE-IDENTICAL artifacts (hash the resolved bytes each path loads) and that retraining 'latest' in place changes the output-schema key. Key files: src/haute/deploy/_validators.py (339-405), src/haute/deploy/_schema.py (74-150), src/haute/deploy/_config.py (~575), src/haute/execution.py (reuse `_stat_gated_runtime_path_fingerprint`), src/haute/_cache.py (371-397), src/haute/_model_scorer.py.

top_changes.title: Encode JSON-shred conservation + fingerprint-completeness as a CHECKED invariant in the wave-2 cache spine (fail-loud-or-account at every loss boundary)

top_changes.title: Cost byte-budget chunk sizing from the TARGET node's projected output schema, not the source schema (close the OOM under-bound)
top_changes.what: C13 is a HIGH OOM hazard on the wave-2 execution surface. I verified the precise mechanism: in `chunking.py`, `_plan_chunk_sizes` (line 593) sizes the chunk from `target_row_bytes = _estimate_projected_row_bytes(target_columns, source_node=..., target_node_id=...)` (line 609), and `_estimate_projected_row_bytes` (line 629) only obtains real widths via `_source_projected_column_widths(source_node, projected_columns)` (line 643) — which RETURNS `{}` for any node whose type is not `DATA_SOURCE` (line 658-659). So for the TARGET node's columns, every downstream-created wide/string column that does not exist on the source falls back to `_DEFAULT_PROJECTED_COLUMN_BYTES` (~64 bytes), and the computed chunk can far exceed the memory budget → OOM. The fix: cost the target row width from the TARGET node's PROJECTED OUTPUT schema — `collect_schema()` on the target lazyframe restricted to `needed_by_node[target]`, sampling String/variable-width columns the way `_source_projected_column_widths` already samples the source (lines 661-687), instead of reading the source schema for target columns. Prioritise this chunk-sizing fix (the HIGH). Treat the second C13 member — the `ExecutionContext` memory limit being a coarse gate sampled only at checkpoint/stage boundaries, so a single ballooning collect/sink between checkpoints is never interrupted — as LOWER priority (L effort): optionally add a bounded-interval watchdog thread per `ExecutionContext` that polls `memory_sampler()` and trips the cancellation token, noting it cannot pre-empt a single in-flight Polars C++ collect (so pair with a hard `process_rss_limit` if pursued). Key files: src/haute/chunking.py (593-687), src/haute/_execution_context.py.
top_changes.why: It is a real OOM (process-killing) hazard with a precise, contained root cause: the chunk planner reasons about the wrong/too-coarse row width for exactly the columns most likely to blow the budget (downstream-created wide strings). The leverage is making memory admission reason about the ACTUAL bytes the target stage materialises, so the budget the planner enforces matches reality — turning a silent OOM under load into a correctly-sized chunk. Self-contained on the wave-2 chunking surface the branch already owns.
